hero.title: A living showcase for modern Angular
hero.description: This boilerplate is designed to stay aligned with the latest Angular capabilities: signal-first state, zoneless change detection, SSR, hydration, incremental hydration, deferrable views and reactive data APIs.

architecture.title: An application foundation, not an empty starter
architecture.description: The boilerplate brings together the infrastructure that repeatedly appears in production Angular applications, while keeping business logic intentionally empty. Every section below is a documented starting point you can fork and extend.

signals.title: Signal-first state
signals.description: Signals, computed state and modern reactive primitives provide a direct model for local and shared application state.

defer.title: Deferrable views
defer.description: The built-in control flow can defer dependencies and hydrate interactive islands only when users need them.

hydration.title: SSR + hydration
hydration.description: Server-rendered HTML becomes interactive in the browser without throwing away the server result.

resources.title: Resource APIs
resources.description: resource() and httpResource() bring asynchronous state into the signal model with loading, error and value states.

forms.title: Signal Forms
forms.description: Angular 22 makes signal-based forms stable, with typed field trees and schema-driven validation.

service.title: Modern DI
service.description: @Service() is the ergonomic root-provided service decorator for the signal-first Angular style.

signals.title: Signals make state explicit
signals.description: The boilerplate favors fine-grained reactivity. signal() owns mutable state, computed() derives state, and newer primitives extend the model to dependent and asynchronous data.
signals.computed: This value is derived automatically from the signal above. No manual change-detection call is required.

rendering.title: Render fast, hydrate intentionally
rendering.description: Angular's modern rendering model combines SSR with hydration and incremental hydration. Deferrable views can keep code out of the critical path while hydrate triggers decide when an island becomes interactive.
rendering.ssrDescription: Render meaningful HTML on the server for fast first paint, SEO and a resilient loading experience.
rendering.hydrationDescription: Angular reuses server-rendered DOM and restores application behavior in the browser. Event replay protects interactions that happen before hydration finishes.
rendering.deferDescription: @defer boundaries can be rendered on the server and hydrated later. Triggers such as viewport, interaction and idle let you move non-critical work away from startup.
rendering.error: The deferred island could not be loaded.
rendering.deferredDescription: This component is intentionally loaded through Angular's deferrable-view pipeline. With incremental hydration, the server can render it while the browser postpones its hydration until the configured trigger fires.
rendering.deferredNote: Signal state survives the hydrated component lifecycle.

data.title: Async data becomes reactive state
data.description: Angular's Resource APIs are now part of the stable signal-based toolbox. Use them when asynchronous values should participate directly in reactive UI state.
data.resource: resource() manages asynchronous operations as a signal-based dependency. It exposes value, status, loading and error state.
data.httpResource: httpResource() builds on HttpClient, so requests remain connected to interceptors and the Angular HTTP stack while exposing their state as signals.
data.linkedSignal: linkedSignal() models writable state that depends on other state, keeping selections and derived choices coherent when their source changes.

forms.title: Forms built on Signals
forms.description: Signal Forms are stable in Angular 22 and are designed for new signal-based applications. A signal model becomes a typed field tree, while schemas centralize validation and reactive field rules.
forms.note: Reactive Forms remain available and are still a strong choice for existing applications. Signal Forms also provide interoperability for gradual migrations.

di.title: Modern dependency injection
di.description: Angular 22 introduces @Service() as the ergonomic shorthand for a root-provided service. It pairs naturally with inject() and avoids the ceremony of @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }) for the common singleton case.
di.note: Keep @Injectable when you need constructor injection, non-root scopes or advanced provider configuration. @Service() is the default style used by this boilerplate.
